data.description:
POST-DEADLINE. Operator ruling 2026-08-12: file, do not work tonight.

SURFACE: /agenda (public day tabs) and /agenda-builder (day selector + grid).

WHAT BREAKS: Day navigation is derived from the conference date window while session data lives in its own window, and the app neither reconciles the two nor warns. During the evaluation the public agenda advertised day tabs 'Wed, May 12 / Thu, May 13 / Fri, May 14' while every session card underneath was dated 'MON, OCT 12' -- so all three day tabs matched zero sessions and ?day=1 and ?day=2 both showed 'No published sessions match', while the All-days view of the same page listed seven sessions. The same divergence emptied the organizer's builder grid: with the DAY selector on 'Wed - May 12', every time x room cell rendered blank though 25 sessions were scheduled.

HONESTY ABOUT PROVENANCE -- THIS WAS SELF-INFLICTED: the evaluation renamed and redated the conference to a fixture, which is what pushed the two windows apart. It is NOT currently reproducible. Verified on live 75b871d94c6f after the demo reset: GET /api/v1/public/agenda returns startsOn 2026-10-12 / endsOn 2026-10-14 with days [Mon Oct 12, Tue Oct 13, Wed Oct 14], and /agenda renders Oct 12/13/14 -- tabs and sessions agree. No judge can hit this without redating the conference themselves.

WHY IT IS STILL A REAL DEFECT: the trigger was artificial, the weakness is not. The product allowed the two windows to diverge, said nothing, and then published day-by-day navigation to attendees that resolved to nothing. An organizer who moves a real conference's dates -- an ordinary thing to do -- silently ships a blank agenda on every day.

FIX SHAPE: on a conference date change, either reconcile scheduled sessions into the new window or refuse silence -- name how many sessions now fall outside it, on the settings surface that made the change and on the builder. A day tab that matches no sessions should say why rather than render an empty programme.

SIZE: medium.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, ai-agenda judgement defects[0] and public-widgets judgement defects[0].
data.title: Conference dates and session dates can diverge silently, publishing day tabs that match nothing

data.body:
REOPENING EVIDENCE — this ticket's own stated premise for deferral is now false, and the defect is live on a public surface during round 9.

MRQ-142 says: 'It is NOT currently reproducible... No judge can hit this without redating the conference themselves.' That was true when filed. It is not true now.

New sighting, reported by #198's owner (surface:102) during visual validation of the seeded build tonight: /agenda renders an empty 'Wed Oct 14' day tab. Nobody redated anything. The conference window is Oct 12-14 — three days, exactly as this ticket verified — and the published program is two days. So the third tab is a container rendered for data that does not exist, reachable by an attendee with one click.

That is the same weakness this ticket describes, arrived at by an ordinary route rather than an artificial one: the date window and the program window do not have to be pushed apart by a rename, they simply are not the same length, which is the normal case for almost every conference that does not fill its last day.

WHAT CHANGES: the deferral rested on 'not reproducible without self-inflicted setup'. It reproduces with no setup at all, on the surface a competition judge opens first, during a scored round. The 11-step walkthrough loop is specified to contain no dead ends and an empty day tab is one.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the operator's ruling of 2026-08-12 said POST-DEADLINE, file, do not work tonight. I am not overriding that on my own authority. I have updated this ticket, not dispatched it, and flagged the call to the merge captain and the operator.

MY RECOMMENDATION on the product question, since it was asked of me: render ALL conference days and say plainly that nothing is scheduled on this one. Do not hide empty days. Hiding them makes the public agenda quietly disagree with the conference's own advertised dates — an attendee who booked a hotel through Oct 14 should not open the programme and see a two-day conference. An empty day that says 'Nothing scheduled on this day yet' is honest, is not a dead end, and costs one line; a missing day is a second, subtler lie. This also matches this ticket's own fix shape ('a day tab that matches no sessions should say why rather than render an empty programme').

NOT the same root as MRQ-176. I checked because it was suggested: MRQ-176's public symptom is one speaker's name missing from one card, which traces to speaker-roster/membership resolution for a hand-added person. This is day-window versus session-window. Two different causes that happen to surface on the same page.

provenance.reason: reproducible on the live public surface during a scored round; deferral premise falsified

data.to:
**Operator ruling 2026-08-14: cleared to build tonight.** The 2026-08-12 "POST-DEADLINE, file, do
not work tonight" deferral is LIFTED — do not stop when you see it in this ticket's history.

## What breaks

Day navigation is derived from the conference date window while session data lives in its own
window, and the app neither reconciles the two nor warns.

**Live today, with no setup at all:** `/agenda` renders an empty **Wed Oct 14** day tab. The
conference window is Oct 12–14 and the published programme is two days, so the third tab is a
container rendered for data that does not exist, reachable by an attendee in one click.

**Original sighting (sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, ai-agenda defects[0] and public-widgets
defects[0]):** the public agenda advertised `Wed, May 12 / Thu, May 13 / Fri, May 14` while every
session card underneath read `MON, OCT 12` — all three tabs matched zero sessions, `?day=1` and
`?day=2` both showed "No published sessions match", and the All-days view of the same page listed
seven sessions. The same divergence emptied the organizer's builder grid: with the DAY selector on
`Wed — May 12`, every time × room cell rendered blank though 25 sessions were scheduled.

## Why the old deferral no longer applies

This ticket deferred itself on the reasoning: *"It is NOT currently reproducible... No judge can
hit this without redating the conference themselves."* That was true when filed and **is false
now.** Nobody redated anything — the date window is simply longer than the programme, which is the
normal case for any conference that does not fill its last day. The artificial trigger was one
route in; ordinary arithmetic is another.

## The product decision — settled, build to it

**Render ALL conference days and say plainly that nothing is scheduled on the empty one. Do not
hide empty days.**

Hiding them makes the public agenda quietly disagree with the conference's own advertised dates.
An attendee who booked a hotel through Oct 14 should not open the programme and find a two-day
conference. **A missing day is a second and subtler lie than an empty one.** An empty day that says
"Nothing scheduled on this day yet" is honest, is not a dead end, and costs one line.

This was put to the operator and not overruled. It also matches this ticket's own original fix
shape.

## What to build

1. **The public agenda renders every day in the conference window.** A day with no published
   sessions states that in the conference's own language rather than rendering an empty programme
   or an unexplained blank.
2. **The same treatment in the agenda builder's DAY selector** — a day with nothing scheduled says
   so rather than showing an empty grid the organizer has to interpret.
3. **A day tab that matches no sessions must never be a dead end.** The 11-step walkthrough loop is
   specified to contain no dead ends, and this is on the first surface a competition judge opens.
4. **Surface the divergence to the organizer when it is real.** On a conference date change, either
   reconcile scheduled sessions into the new window or **refuse silence**: name how many sessions
   now fall outside it, on the settings surface that made the change and on the builder. An
   organizer who moves a real conference's dates — an ordinary thing to do — currently ships a
   blank agenda on every day and is told nothing.
5. **Elements never jump** — the empty-day copy must occupy the space a populated day would, so
   switching tabs does not reflow the page.

## Acceptance

- With a conference window longer than its programme, every day tab renders and the empty one
  states that nothing is scheduled. **Pair it:** assert in the same response that a populated day
  still lists its sessions, so "everything is empty" cannot pass for "the empty day is labelled".
- No day tab is a dead end.
- Changing the conference dates so sessions fall outside the window produces a stated count on the
  settings surface and the builder, not silence.
- Regression test red on `main`, green on the branch, covering the public agenda and the builder.

## Constraints

- Cut your worktree from `github/main`. CLAUDE.md now carries the correct instruction and the
  primary checkout has been fast-forwarded, so follow the file. Verify anyway:
  `if git fetch github; then if git merge-base --is-ancestor github/main HEAD; then echo current; else echo 'behind -- rebase'; fi; else echo 'FETCH FAILED -- not attempted'; fi`
- **Never `git stash` anywhere in this repo** — the stash stack is shared across every worktree.
- **Push when the work is written, before the verification run.** Every agent that has stalled on
  this project ran out during final verification, with the work finished and unpushed. A green gate
  on unpushed work is worth nothing to a successor; the verification can be re-run by anyone, the
  work cannot.
- **Confirm the instrument before believing a NEGATIVE browser result.** A dead or stale local
  Worker produces exactly the symptoms of a broken change. `lsof -i :<port>`, then
  `curl -s localhost:<port>/health` and compare its `build` field (12 chars, root path) against
  `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD`. Better still, pair every absence with a positive from the same
  response.
- Gate through `/Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/.gate-lock/gate-lock.sh`.
- Test titles start with `CONTRACT` or `AC-<n>`, then a middle dot.
- No migration without the operator. **Do not deploy** — deploys are queued and coordinated by the
  merge captain.

Provenance: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34; re-sighted live on the round-9 build by #198's owner,
2026-08-14.

data.body: Root cause: public and builder day navigation used only the conference date window while sessions could be on different dates, and neither surface reported the divergence or provided an empty-day recovery state. Verified: npx vitest run tests/unit/conference-dates.MRQ-142.test.ts tests/unit/agenda-click-to-place.MRQ-141.test.ts tests/integration/public-site.AC-83-86-240-252-253.test.ts tests/integration/api/agenda.AC-70-74-252-253.test.ts tests/integration/api/event-settings.test.ts was red before the fix and passed with 40 tests after it; npx tsc --noEmit passed; /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/.gate-lock/gate-lock.sh npm run pr-gate -- --ticket MRQ-142 passed. PR #220.

Independent review — agent:eval-triage (workspace:10), merge owner. Reviewed by surface:178 (APPROVE) and by me as a non-author; merged as PR #220, bcc4d68b27e6.

This ticket was filed 2026-08-12 and deferred by an operator ruling — POST-DEADLINE, file, do not work tonight — on the stated premise that it was 'NOT currently reproducible... No judge can hit this without redating the conference themselves.' That premise went false: nobody redated anything, the conference window is simply Oct 12-14 while the published programme is two days, so the third tab was empty by ordinary arithmetic on the first surface a competition judge opens. I put the changed premise to the operator rather than overriding the ruling myself, and Atin cleared it tonight.

Before dispatching I rewrote the ticket body, because it still LED with the deferral. A fresh agent reads 'do not work tonight' and stops — correctly, since it is obeying the most authoritative-looking line in its brief. The dispatch would have failed silently and looked like an idle agent.

The review ran the two checks that mattered on an 18-file diff for a defect that sounds like one line:

  reverted the fix and watched the new tests go red — so the coverage is real rather than described
  confirmed all five MODIFIED EXISTING tests are legitimate fixture adaptations, not weakened
    assertions — which is where a regression hides in plain sight

And it settled the scope question I could not answer from the ticket: the event-settings change is ROOT CAUSE rather than creep. It warns the organizer when a session falls outside the conference window, which is the condition that produced the empty tab. That is the fourth acceptance item — refuse silence when the two windows diverge — rather than an unrelated addition.

Behaviour matches the ruling as written: renders ALL conference days, labels the empty one, never hides it. The reasoning was kept in the ticket deliberately so nobody would optimise it into 'hiding empty days is tidier' — an attendee who booked a hotel through Oct 14 should not open the programme and find a two-day conference.
